final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded the core missing predicates: no approved pre-launch risk acceptance, no reviewed mitigation, and no attached disclosure language for the current named-use-case regression. Aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, general governance guidance, and prior approval context support a narrow operational-readiness narrative, but they do not satisfy the certification policy requirement that current release documentation reflect current evaluation results and that material segment weaknesses be disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. That distinction matters: a caveated certification position may be rhetorically narrower than a clean compliance claim, but here the caveat itself identifies an unresolved compliance predicate rather than merely tempering confidence. The Actor mainly reframed the same record and narrowed the claim; that does not cure the underlying policy failure.
remaining_concerns: The current loan modification support slice is 1.4 percentage points below the warning threshold for a named launch use case.
The record still contains no attached disclosure language, approved pre-launch risk acceptance, or reviewed mitigation for that weakness.
Policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses to be disclosed or covered by approved mitigation before certification.
Prior approval of the same model family predates the current retrieval configuration change and current evaluation batch, so it cannot satisfy the current-release documentation requirement.
The informal post-launch monitoring comment remains contextual only and does not satisfy the policy predicate.
